findings.title: stream_close() gates stop()/abort() behind an unbounded queue drain
findings.claim: stop()'s abort() is chained strictly after the new outgoing-queue drain wait, but abort() is the only mechanism that can fail a stuck low-level write; if a frame is parked on peer backpressure, queue_drained never resolves and the connection's fd, buffers, and teardown state leak forever with no timeout or cancellation.

findings.title: Exceptional queue-drain branch in stream_close() has no test coverage
findings.claim: The then_wrapped/ignore_ready_future() branch that keeps stream_close() completing when a queued send failed is never exercised because the new test only ever queues an eof marker that always succeeds; a future regression letting the exception propagate or skipping write_buf.close() on that path would hang teardown undetected.

findings.title: New doxygen block leaves a stale duplicate one-line comment beneath it on sink and source
findings.claim: The new /// \brief blocks on sink (:337-343) and source (:384-390) are stacked directly on top of the retained one-line comments, so each class carries two unsynced descriptions, unlike every other documented entity in the header.

findings.title: Unguarded put(std::span) override breaks compilation at SEASTAR_API_LEVEL < 9
findings.claim: test_data_sink_impl's put(std::span) override isn't guarded by SEASTAR_API_LEVEL, but at API level 7 or 8 data_sink_impl has no such overload (only put(net::packet)), so the override matches nothing and the class stays abstract, breaking the build at those levels which CMakeLists.txt still offers.

findings.title: Regression test swallows closed_error from send() without asserting it
findings.claim: The refused send()'s closed_error is caught by a bare try/catch and discarded with nothing asserted, so the test's only real signal is an indirect timing-dependent check (put_after_close) that can pass even if the fix regresses, if the batch-flush poller happens to run within a fixed yield budget.

findings.title: Test releases parked close() only on the happy path, so unexpected exceptions hang to timeout
findings.claim: st.release_close.set_value() sits on the straight-line happy path after the try/catch, so any exception other than closed_error escaping the guarded region leaves the connection blocked in output_stream::close() and stop_send_loop(), wedging the test until the 300s harness timeout instead of failing cleanly.

findings.title: Whether real-world compressors tolerate send() now returning closed_error broadly is unverified
findings.claim: connection::send() now returns closed_error once _stream_closing is set for any caller, not just sink-guarded ones, and whether every real-world compressor calling send_empty_frame tolerates an exceptional returned future could not be verified from the repository alone.

findings.title: stream_close()/stop_send_loop() interleaving safety depends on an undocumented ordering assumption
findings.claim: The interleaving is safe only because stop_send_loop() sets _error = true synchronously with no suspension point before the when_all at :225; a future co_await or early return between those points would let stream_close()'s if (!error()) guard fail to protect the new std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, ...) from a moved-from future, and nothing in the code records this dependency.

findings.title: _connected dereferenced unguarded, asymmetric with stop_send_loop()'s guarded check
findings.claim: Line 569 dereferences _connected unguarded where stop_send_loop() guards the same call with _connected && at :231; no path disengaging _connected after set_socket() was found, but the call is now deferred behind a scheduling point and the asymmetry is unexplained.

findings.title: Test's test_sink_state captured by reference may outlive RPC-internal shared_ptr teardown
findings.claim: st is captured by reference by objects whose lifetime follows RPC-internal shared_ptr refcounting rather than C++ scope; declaring st first is protective only if dropping sink and source synchronously releases the last reference.

findings.title: close_entered_cv.wait() has no timeout, so a regression hangs instead of failing cleanly
findings.claim: st.close_entered_cv.wait(...) at :2011 has no timeout, so a regression preventing stream_close() from being entered hangs the test rather than failing it cleanly.

findings.title: Class-level doxygen states the close contract but sink::close() itself still lacks it
findings.claim: The new class-level doxygen on rpc::sink states the close contract, but sink::close() itself (unchanged by this diff) still carries only its one-line comment, so a reader who opens the method rather than the class banner does not see the contract.

findings.title: Test's server-handler read loop may raise stream_closed during normal shutdown and escape server_done.get()
findings.claim: Peer claim: while (source().get()) {} in the new test's server handler may raise rpc::stream_closed during normal client-side shutdown and escape server_done.get() at :2028; retained as risk only, with no demonstrated trigger since the file's stream_closed precedent covers reads issued past end-of-stream and this loop stops at the first unengaged optional.

findings.title: Peer drain exception may escape regression test teardown
findings.claim: A single-source peer finding held that a peer drain exception escapes the regression test's teardown; demoted to residual risk as advisory-routed, with no violated contract quoted and no current user-facing defect.

findings.title: No test drives the outgoing queue to be non-ready when stream_close() runs
findings.claim: No test drives _outgoing_queue_ready to be non-ready at the moment stream_close() runs, so neither a chain walk over several in-flight frames nor an entry stuck on peer backpressure (the trigger for finding #1) is covered.

findings.title: No test covers stop_send_loop() running concurrently with a parked stream_close()
findings.claim: No test covers stop_send_loop() running concurrently with a parked stream_close(); a peer reset while stream_close() waits on queued_drained would exercise exactly the serialization this diff rewrites between :225-231 and :562-570.
